key_claims: AI coding raises pull request arrival rate faster than teams can review, producing queues, bigger batches, rubber-stamp approvals and concentrated cognitive load on a few reviewers. This is a constraint shift, not an AI failure. Apply Theory of Constraints five focusing steps: identify review as the constraint, exploit it (agent-prepared review packets with goals, approved specs, risk areas, test evidence, suggested review paths; agent pre-reviews; small batches), subordinate (limit WIP so that when the limit is reached teams stop starting and start finishing), elevate (add review capacity only when it raises validated business throughput), repeat. An 'SDD Kanban view' tracks each feature/spec from intent to validation using WIP, work item age, blocked markers and cumulative flow. Review plans/specs before code to catch wrong direction without recreating waterfall. Suggested metrics (per search summary, not confirmed in fetch): review queue size, time to first meaningful review, PR age, batch size, rework after review, reviewer concentration. The 9 June post argues spec-driven development is a higher-level language, backlog items carry intent while detailed specs are written during execution by builders, and Kanban visualises where review backs up.

Lead check: the lead said Yeret proposes SDD Kanban boards that expose review inventory and force teams to stop starting new AI sessions, and applies WIP limits to review. Broadly matches: the SDD Kanban view and 'stop starting and start finishing' are in the 15 June post, but 'new AI prompting sessions' is not his wording as far as seen. The 9 June post does not use the term 'WIP limits', only 'Limit work in process'. [uncertain]
sample_and_method: No sample or method. Support is anecdotal: a Reddit question from a founder, conversations with scaled engineering organisations and CI/CD practitioners, and the author's observations of internal and public repositories. Uncited 'I'm seeing engineering organizations...' statements in the 9 June post.
limitations: Opinion and practitioner reasoning applied from Theory of Constraints, not empirical evidence. No data, no named organisations, no before/after results. Anecdotes are unquantified and unverifiable. Author has consulting interest. Quotes come via a summarising fetch tool; original site not opened directly. Does not address whether review quality (versus throughput) improves under WIP limits.
what_a_leader_can_do: Treat review as the system constraint: make review queue visible on a flow board, set a WIP limit on work waiting for or in review and enforce stop-starting, shrink batch size, require review packets and spec/plan review before code, and fund review capacity only when it raises delivered business throughput. Evidence strength: weak (reasoned from TOC and anecdote, no measurements), though TOC and Kanban WIP logic is long established in lean literature.
overlap_with_site_essays: Strong overlap with Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part (concentrated reviewer load) and The Verification Gap (review as the limiting step). Moderate with What It Takes to Trust Agent Output (review packets, test evidence). Little with Checking Isn't Catching, since Yeret addresses throughput and queues, not whether reviewers catch defects. Yeret supplies the leadership/flow-management framing those essays may lack, but only as opinion.
